subject: MAP checkpoint — GPU runway and regional throughput for Dedicated/Private

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP checkpoint — GPU runway and regional throughput for Dedicated/Private

Hi Priya —

Following up on last week's MAP sprint: we want to lock the Dedicated/Private sizing assumptions so procurement and infra can start the reserve flows. Summary ask below and attached an updated MAP workbook (AtlasRx_MAP_v2.xlsx) that mirrors the items. Please confirm by EOD Monday if the numbers look right or flag changes.

Key ask (proposed):
- GPU mix (initial): 6 x A100 80GB (us-east1), 4 x H100 (us-west2), 2 x A10G (for lower-cost burst).
- Target throughput: 120 concurrent inference workers (~180 seq/s aggregate for the primary LLM), peak 2.5M tokens/day.
- Regions: primary=us-east1, DR=us-west2.
- Timeline: pilot (1 node pool) in dev by 2027-04-15, production rollout + SLA by 2027-06-30.

Open / uncertain items we need your confirmation on:
1) GPU preference — you previously mentioned comfort with H100 for the highest-accuracy route but wanted to keep A100 for cost parity. If you confirm, we will build a mixed pool and run perf tests.
2) Regions — is us-west2 mandatory for DR or would eu-west also be useful for latency to EU customers?
3) Throughput targets — please confirm peak traffic windows (timezone/weekday patterns) so we can size autoscaling.

Action items proposed (owners in parentheses):
- Priya: confirm GPU mix + peak windows (Priya Shah) — due Mon 2027-03-08
- Laura: prepare pricing delta for A100 vs H100 reservations (Laura Bennett) — due Wed 2027-03-10
- Dylan: perf test plan + KV cache targets (Dylan Brooks) — due Fri 2027-03-12
- Camila: schedule technical sync (Camila Reyes) — sched invite pending

Attachments: AtlasRx_MAP_v2.xlsx, region-throughput-proposal.pdf

Thanks — want to make sure MAP milestones align with your procurement window. If you prefer, we can do a 30-min call early next week to walk the workbook.

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasrx.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasRx Sales <sales@atlasrx.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — GPU runway and regional throughput for Dedicated/Private

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick answers inline.

- GPU mix: Confirmed on mixed pool. Preference is H100 for the accuracy-critical inference (we expect ~40% of requests to hit the high-accuracy path). A100 80GB for baseline; keep A10G as optional for non-peak bursts.
- Regions: DR in us-west2 is fine. We do want an EU presence later in Q3 but that can be a phase 2 (not blocking).
- Throughput / patterns: Primary traffic 06:00-18:00 PT weekdays, with peaks on Monday mornings. Peak token estimate of 2.2-2.8M/day is correct.

Procurement note: procurement lead indicated a typical 6-8 week approval for reserved capacity if pricing is final, but we can fast-track with a PO hold if Redwood can provide a firm pricing delta and SKU commitment by 2027-03-12.

I attached our internal ops notes (see region-throughput-proposal.pdf) that call out special encryption controls for EU users (relevant for phase 2).

Priya Shah
Head of Platform Ops, AtlasRx
priya.shah@atlasrx.ai | +1 650-555-0133

Great, thanks Priya — that helps a lot. Notes from our side after reviewing pricing and infra windows:

1) Pricing delta (preliminary):
   - A100 80GB reserved: baseline unit price.
   - H100 reserved: ~22% premium vs. A100 (we'll provide exact SKU pricing by EOD 3/12).
   - A10G burst: negligible incremental cost for on-demand burst pools.

2) Recommended commit plan (to meet your timeline):
   - Phase A (pilot): reserve 4 x A100 + 2 x H100 for pilot cluster (dev/staging) — start by 2027-04-05.
   - Phase B (production): scale to 6 x A100 + 4 x H100 by 2027-06-15 pending perf results and PO.

3) Capacity / throughput notes (for Dylan): run perf tests using 1.5x expected peak token rate and validate KV cache hit targets >= 70% to meet latency SLOs.
